title: Queue slip & KV thrash — OOM diagnostic diary
content:
Summary:

This is an on-call diagnostic diary for a multi-host memory escalation we observed on 2024-11-05 that manifested as progressive OOMs and host restarts across a subset of serving hosts running continuous batching and aggressive prefetching. Symptoms were gradual heap growth (minutes -> tens of minutes), long GC stalls, and a correlated spike in kv_cache.memory_bytes and batch_queue.depth.

This doc captures the timeline, hypotheses, triage commands, immediate mitigations we executed, proposed runbook items, and follow-up engineering actions. Aim is to turn this into a short, actionable runbook (see "Runbook draft" section) and an investigation checklist for SRE + serving-runtime.

High-level symptom list:
- Hosts slowly hit RSS/heap OOMs rather than sudden peaks.
- Continuous batching tail latency climbs then queue depth explodes.
- KV cache size increases and does not reclaim entries quickly.
- Prefetch worker counts spike on affected hosts.
- Partial batch failures leave batches in "zombie" state with references to big prefix objects.

Immediate timeline (UTC):
- 2024-11-05 02:12 — First alert: host-a-15 reported OOM and restarted.
- 2024-11-05 02:15 — host-a-18 and host-b-02 showed similar restarts within 3 minutes.
- 2024-11-05 02:17 — SRE oncall (Aisha) paged. Began triage: Prometheus queries, heap profiles, pstack traces.
- 2024-11-05 02:32 — Mitigation: throttled prefetcher at dyndynconfig=0.35 (reduced parallel prefetch per-request).
- 2024-11-05 02:39 — Additional mitigation: disabled continuous batching on the affected allocation pool, rerouted to microbatch fallback.
- 2024-11-05 03:10 — Observed memory usage stabilizing on previously offlined hosts; restarts stopped after throttles applied.
- 2024-11-05 04:00 — Post-incident: snapshot heap profiles stored to S3. Created ticket SRE-7912 for root cause investigation.

What we saw in the data (evidence):
- Prometheus snippets used during triage (copy of queries):
  - sum by(instance) (process_resident_memory_bytes{job="serving-runtime"})
  - increase(kv_cache_entries_total[15m]) > 1000 on affected hosts.
  - histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(batch_processing_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
  - rate(prefetch_worker_spawn_count[1m]) spiking to 40+ on some hosts.

- pprof heap snapshots: dominant objects attributed to PrefixBuffer and PrefetchBuffer slices; many live objects referenced from batch_shard structs.
- GDB/backtrace of stuck thread: stuck in prefetch::fill_prefetch_buffer() and then re-entered by batch_completion callback without properly releasing ownership.
- Logs: repeated warnings like "prefetch: partial fill, error code=TIMEOUT, retaining partial buffers for retry" followed by batch requeue.

Hypotheses (ordered by confidence):
1) Prefetch partial-failure path leaks buffer references: when a prefetch times out we keep a partial PrefixBuffer in memory attached to a requeued batch; if batch is retried many times buffers accumulate. Evidence: heap shows many small but live PrefixBuffer objects with batch_id tags.
2) Continuous batching scheduler's sliding-window accounting doesn't cap combined memory across inflight prefetches and KV cache entries. Combined effect allows queue to slip past safe limits when latency increases.
3) A race between batch cancelation and KV cache insertion: canceled prefetch still writes a KV entry (duplicate key variant) and increments kv_cache.entry_ref without decrementing on cancel. Leads to kv_cache.count drift and eviction not triggered.

Immediate mitigations we executed (and rationale):
- Throttle prefetch parallelism (dyndynconfig to 0.35): reduced concurrent prefetch memory footprint and gave the system headroom.
- Disable continuous batching for affected allocation pool (fallback to microbatch): reduced single-host aggregation and prevented large sliding-window growth.
- Increase eviction aggressiveness (kv_cache.eviction_threshold -20%): forced more aggressive reclaiming while we probed leak.
- Remove hosts from LB rotation where heap profiles looked anomalous and marked for controlled restart.

Triage commands and scripts we ran (for reproducibility):
- curl -s "http://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=sum%20process_resident_memory_bytes%7Bjob%3D%5C"serving-runtime%5C"%7D%20by%20(instance)" | jq .
- go tool pprof -alloc_space http://host-a-15:6060/debug/pprof/heap > heap-host-a-15.pb.gz
- sudo journalctl -u serving-runtime -S "2024-11-05 02:00" -U "2024-11-05 04:00" --no-pager | grep -E "prefetch|batch|kv_cache"
- python scripts/inspect_batch_zombies.py --input heap-host-a-15.pb.gz --out /tmp/zombie-report.txt

Runbook draft (short, actionable) — target for SRE-runbook conversion:
Detection rules (alerts):
- A1: host_resident_memory > host_mem_limit * 0.9 for 3m -> page oncall.
- A2: rate(kv_cache_entries_added[10m]) > 500 and kv_cache_evictions_rate < 1 -> warning.
- A3: batch_queue.depth > 200 on a single host for 5m -> escalate.

Immediate remediation steps (order matters):
1) If A1 or A3: remove host from rotation: /bin/drain_host --host <instance> --reason "OOM-queue-slip".
2) Apply dyndynconfig throttles: curl -XPOST https://controlplane/api/dyndyn/config -d '{"prefetch_parallelism":0.35}' (ops-only).
3) If memory not stabilizing after throttles (10m): disable continuous batching for pool: /bin/flip_feature --pool <pool> --feature continuous_batching --off.
4) Force a controlled restart after clearing ephemeral buffers: ssh host; kill -SIGTERM $(pidof serving-runtime); wait for orderly shutdown and capture final heap.
5) If kv_cache.evictions_rate is very low but entries keep increasing, trigger manual evictions: curl -XPOST https://serving-runtime/api/admin/kv/evict?percent=20

How to validate we've killed the leak:
- Watch sum(process_resident_memory_bytes) go flat or decline for 15m.
- kv_cache_entries_total stops monotonically increasing and evictions pick up.
- No new "partial buffer retained" logs after throttles.

Post-incident engineering action items (owners + rough ETA):
- ENG-SR-1 (Jonas) — Add guard in prefetch partial-failure path to always release buffer ownership and add a metric prefetch.partial_leak_count (ETA 2d).
- ENG-SR-2 (Maya) — Fix sliding-window accounting to include estimated prefetch memory and kv_cache footprint; add unit tests + integration test scenario (ETA 1w).
- ENG-SR-3 (Luis) — Add an e2e chaos test: simulate prefetch timeout + retry storm to ensure no unbounded memory accumulation (ETA 2w).
- ENG-SR-4 (Aisha) — Convert this doc into SRE runbook page and wire alerts A1/A2/A3 (ETA 3d).
- ENG-SR-5 (Platform) — Add a safe kill switch to auto-disable continuous batching when host-level memory crosses threshold for multiple hosts in pool (design review in 1w).

Open questions / follow-ups we still need to answer:
- Exact leak path: is it purely code-path leak in prefetch, or also an accounting bug in kv_cache that prevents eviction decisions? Heap shows both.
- Does the batching sliding-window mis-estimate memory because it assumes cached prefixes are pinned to model shards rather than per-request?
- Could we add a soft memory watermark at batch-scheduler level that rejects new requests when combined estimated inflight memory > host_budget?

Notes-to-self / investigative clues that were helpful:
- pprof object labels included batch_id which made it easy to map live objects to batch traces. We should ensure pprof labels are present in builds.
- The 'partial buffer retained' log line was introduced in PR 4132; look at that code for error-return path.
- Hostset pattern: affected hosts had slightly older kernel (5.10.0-42) and a different jemalloc version; low confidence correlation but worth standardizing.

Appendix: quick references for oncall
- script to list batches by age: scripts/list_inflight_batches.sh --host <inst>
- one-liner to force kv eviction: curl -XPOST http://localhost:8080/admin/kv/evict?percent=30
- pprof endpoint: http://<host>:6060/debug/pprof/heap (remember to capture with go tool pprof -alloc_space)

Log snippets (sanitized):
- "WARN prefetch: partial fill, error=TIMEOUT, batch_id=bf2c1a, retained=2/8 buffers"
- "DEBUG batch-scheduler: sliding_window_size=128 mem_est=2.6GB inflight_prefetch_mem=1.8GB"
- "ERROR kv-cache: insert failed(key=prefix-xyz) but ref_count incremented"

If you pick this up: please add findings & any small repro steps here. Next sync: eng-sre standup 2024-11-14 (agenda: confirm owners, merge quick guard PRs, draft runbook page).

End of diary.
